episode_title: AI Governance as an MSP Revenue Opportunity | Josh Coke and Sunny Kaila

real_qa.q: Why is AI-powered cybersecurity becoming a major revenue opportunity for MSPs compared to traditional security services?
real_qa.r: For the first time in 20 years, end clients are proactively asking MSPs how they can use AI, rather than MSPs having to sell security services to reluctant small businesses. MSPs can respond to this customer demand by packaging AI governance as a service and AI preparedness using Microsoft Purview, DLP, and sensitivity labeling—enabling security rollouts that deliver productivity gains while protecting data.

real_qa.q: What governance and data protection foundations must be in place before enabling Microsoft Copilot in a tenant?
real_qa.r: Copilot works within your existing Microsoft tenant access rules and permissions. If your tenant has sprawl and uncontrolled access, Copilot will expose that information to anyone who asks—employees can retrieve salary data, HR complaints, or confidential files they shouldn't access. Setting up sensitivity labels and data protection policies through Microsoft Purview is essential, and for small businesses, this can now be configured in an afternoon rather than requiring massive enterprise-level projects.
real_qa.requete: Copilot Microsoft Purview data governance setup

real_qa.q: What is the three-question framework that MSPs should apply to justify any AI or technology investment?
real_qa.r: The three questions are: Does this help me increase revenue, decrease cost, or mitigate risk? If you don't have a yes to any of those three, it's probably not a justifiable expense. The more yeses you get, the more strongly you should lean into the investment—whether for AI tools, equipment, or other business initiatives.
real_qa.requete: three questions justify technology investment revenue cost risk

real_qa.q: How should MSPs structure their first 90-day AI activation plan for customers?
real_qa.r: Start with the customer's desired outcome and define success metrics—whether they want to improve quality, speed, or buy back time (QST framework). Then reverse-engineer the use cases and governance requirements needed to achieve that outcome. Begin with a clear outcome, align the activation plan around business results, and ensure governance and security are the foundation of the entire journey.
real_qa.requete: 90 day AI activation plan MSP customers outcome

real_qa.q: How is Enforcer using AI internally to improve product development and customer responsiveness?
real_qa.r: Enforcer uses AI note takers on customer and prospect calls, then deploys agents to analyze transcripts for sentiment, competitor mentions, and specific problems customers describe. This generates weekly summaries showing real-time demand and friction points, allowing the product team to respond instantly to customer needs without relying on traditional focus groups.
real_qa.requete: AI note takers customer call analysis product development

guest.bio_context: Josh has worked in the MSP space for 20 years, starting at Kaseya in 2006 during the early days of RMM technology. He later brought Autotask's RMM tool from the UK to the United States and worked through multiple acquisitions including Datto acquiring Autotask and Kaseya acquiring Datto. He joined Enforcer's founders (Rich, Will, and Jamie) to expand their tenant management solution into the U.S. market.
